_comment: Every paper already triaged. The daily watch normalizes candidate titles (lowercase, alphanumerics + single spaces) and skips any whose title_norm already appears in in_scope or excluded. New, in-scope titles get a note in papers/ and a new in_scope entry.

excluded.title: Experimental Security Analysis of the App Model in Business Collaboration Platforms
excluded.title_norm: experimental security analysis of the app model in business collaboration platforms
excluded.reason: Studies the server-side third-party app permission model of Slack/Teams; no Electron client / renderer / IPC angle despite Slack & Teams being Electron apps.

excluded.title: Identity Confusion in WebView-based Mobile App-in-app Ecosystems
excluded.title_norm: identity confusion in webview-based mobile app-in-app ecosystems
excluded.reason: WebView app-in-app security, but explicitly mobile (super-apps); desktop/Electron out of scope. Conceptually adjacent only.

excluded.title: Jack-in-the-box: An Empirical Study of JavaScript Bundling on the Web and its Security Implications
excluded.title_norm: jack-in-the-box an empirical study of javascript bundling on the web and its security implications
excluded.reason: Pure web study of JavaScript bundlers; no desktop/Electron angle.

excluded.title: webFuzz: Grey-Box Fuzzing for Web Applications
excluded.title_norm: webfuzz grey-box fuzzing for web applications
excluded.reason: Server-side web-application fuzzing; no desktop privilege escalation / Electron angle.

excluded.title: On the Feasibility of Cross-Language Detection of Malicious Packages in npm and PyPI
excluded.title_norm: on the feasibility of cross-language detection of malicious packages in npm and pypi
excluded.reason: Generic npm/PyPI supply-chain detection; not Electron/desktop-app specific. Borderline — promote only if the thesis has a broad supply-chain section.

excluded.title: Cross-Boundary Mobile Tracking: Exploring Java-to-JavaScript Information Diffusion in WebViews
excluded.title_norm: cross-boundary mobile tracking exploring java-to-javascript information diffusion in webviews
excluded.reason: WebView Java-to-JS information-flow tracking, but explicitly mobile (Android in-app browsers / tracking-privacy); no desktop/Electron renderer/IPC angle.

excluded.title: From Noise to Signal: Precisely Identify Affected Packages of Known Vulnerabilities in npm Ecosystem
excluded.title_norm: from noise to signal precisely identify affected packages of known vulnerabilities in npm ecosystem
excluded.reason: Generic npm vulnerability-to-package mapping / SCA accuracy; not Electron- or Node.js-runtime-vulnerability-discovery specific (same rationale as the excluded npm/PyPI detection paper).

excluded.title: FirmCross: Detecting Taint-style Vulnerabilities in Modern C-Lua Hybrid Web Services of Linux-based Firmware
excluded.title_norm: firmcross detecting taint-style vulnerabilities in modern c-lua hybrid web services of linux-based firmware
excluded.reason: Matched on 'hybrid' but targets C-Lua hybrid web services in Linux-based firmware (embedded/IoT), not a hybrid web/desktop (Electron) app.

excluded.title: Original Sin of npm: A Study on Vulnerability Propagation in JavaScript Dependency Networks
excluded.title_norm: original sin of npm a study on vulnerability propagation in javascript dependency networks
excluded.reason: Generic npm/JavaScript dependency-network vulnerability-propagation measurement (1,515 vulns across ~1.08M packages); empirical SCA, not Electron- or Node.js-runtime-vulnerability-DISCOVERY specific. Same rationale as the excluded 'From Noise to Signal' (NDSS'26) and 'Cross-Language Detection of Malicious Packages' (ACSAC'23).

context_non_venue.title: Electrolint and security of electron applications
context_non_venue.why: Most-cited non-top-venue Electron static-analysis work (client-side XSS, clickjacking, DOM clobbering in Electron apps). Use if broadening beyond the 9 venues.

context_non_venue.title: ElectroVolt: Pwning popular desktop apps while uncovering new attack surface on Electron
context_non_venue.why: Industry research (not peer-reviewed). Widely cited 1-click RCE chains in Discord, Teams, VS Code, Element. Good motivation / real-world impact citation.

context_non_venue.title: Developers Are Victims Too: A Comprehensive Analysis of the VS Code Extension Ecosystem
context_non_venue.why: Security of the VS Code (Electron) extension ecosystem. Preprint — confirm any venue acceptance before citing as published.

context_non_venue.title: JavaSith: A Client-Side Framework for Analyzing Potentially Malicious Extensions in Browsers, VS Code, and NPM Packages
context_non_venue.why: Client-side analysis spanning browsers, VS Code, and npm. Preprint — verify status before citing.
